\section{Overview}
The input moment conditions for fourth-order invariance are packaged together and shown to depend only on the input distribution.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Fourth-order invariance moment conditions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsBReasonable}
Let $X$ be a real function on a measured space $(\Omega,\mu)$. It satisfies the invariance moment conditions when $\mu$ is a probability measure, $X$ is measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, $\mathbb E X=\mathbb E X^3=0$, $\mathbb E X^2=1$, and $\mathbb E X^4\le9$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Transfer of invariance moments by distribution]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments.identDistrib}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be real random variables on measured spaces $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$, where $\nu$ is a probability measure. If $X$ satisfies the invariance moment conditions and $X$ and $Y$ have the same distribution, then $Y$ is measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment and moments $\mathbb EY=\mathbb EY^3=0$, $\mathbb EY^2=1$, and $\mathbb EY^4\le9$; thus $Y$ satisfies the same moment conditions.
\end{theorem}
